name: Coordinated Inauthentic Behavior
description: Detection and analysis of coordinated link-sharing, inauthentic networks, and manipulated amplification on social media, including the CooRnet/CLSB methodology and its successors. This is the researcher's signature methodological contribution and remains central to current publications and tools (VERA-AI Alert, coordinated network studies in Italy, Germany, Nigeria, India, Brazil).

name: Information Disorder & Disinformation
description: Broad research line on mis/disinformation, fake news taxonomies, problematic information circulation, and deceptive information operations, spanning war/health/political contexts; underpins the PROMPT and MINE-FACTS projects and numerous recent papers on 'zombie internet' and iterative deception.

name: Generative AI & Synthetic Media Manipulation
description: Emerging focus on how generative AI tools are used for persuasion, deception, and manipulation—e.g., synthetic visuals in gambling promotion, AI-generated disinformation, and deepfakes—reflecting a rapidly growing current agenda area (2025-2026 book chapters and news items).

name: Platform Data Access & Governance
description: Critical examination of social media research infrastructures, API access, the Digital Services Act, and the consequences of platform policy changes (e.g., CrowdTangle shutdown, Meta's URL Shares Dataset, political content reduction policies) for both research methodology and democratic accountability.

name: Italian Political Communication & Elections
description: Long-running empirical research on Italian media and social media dynamics around national elections (2018, 2022) and political actors, including partisan attention, hyperpartisan networks, and parliamentary visibility—core to the MINE programme since its founding.

name: Computational Methods & LLMs for Content Analysis
description: Methodological work on applying large language models and embedding techniques to classify and annotate political and social media text at scale, including validation challenges of LLM-in-the-loop pipelines—an active and growing methodological concern.

name: Political Polarization & Partisan Engagement
description: Study of affective and structural polarization, partisan community dynamics, and algorithmic/media amplification of extremes, connecting historical work on media insularity with recent longitudinal analyses of partisan Facebook networks (e.g., pro-Bolsonaro communities).

name: Health Misinformation & Coordinated Networks
description: Investigation of coordinated circulation of problematic health information, notably COVID-19 and broader health content in India and Nigeria, funded by the Gates Foundation and MUR, connecting platform analysis with public health communication concerns.

name: Cross-National Digital Campaign Analysis
description: Comparative studies of political information campaigns and coordinated behavior across national election contexts (Germany 2021, Brazil, Latin America), reflecting the researcher's expanding international collaborative network beyond Italy.

name: Public and Sociotechnical Approaches to AI Safety Evaluation
description: Papers framing AI safety practices—red-teaming and evaluation—as sociotechnical activities requiring public involvement, labor consideration, and participatory science methods rather than purely technical procedures.

name: Online Radicalization and Extremism Across Platforms
description: Empirical and review studies of how extremist actors (far-right, jihadist) exploit platform affordances, algorithms, and multimodal content to spread and normalize radical ideologies online.

name: Retrospective Essays on Platformization and Social Media's Trajectory
description: Reflective anniversary/position essays diagnosing the current state of social media and platform economies, tracing how platformization, political economy, and scam/extractive logics have reshaped online life over the past decade.

name: Public Attitudes and Labor Experiences with AI
description: Survey- and discourse-based studies of how publics and workers perceive, use, and are shaped by AI systems, including stakeholder discourse, national attitudes, and worker-reported productivity and displacement effects.

name: LLMs and Computational Methods for Research Workflows
description: Methodological papers deploying LLMs or fine-tuned models to augment scholarly tasks such as peer review, qualitative coding, and domain-specific classification, with attention to human-in-the-loop design and evaluation.

name: Message-Based Interventions for Climate Communication and Misinformation Resistance
description: Experimental and review studies testing how framed messages, chatbots, or inoculation techniques shape audience attitudes, resistance to misinformation, and engagement with climate or conspiracy content.

name: Survey Data Quality, Comprehension, and Recruitment
description: Papers examining the methodological foundations of online survey research, including whether respondents understand survey questions as intended, how representative and valid different opt-in sample sources are, and how novel platform-based recruitment strategies (e.g., Facebook ads) can be used and evaluated for reaching hard-to-survey populations.

name: Computational Approaches to Social Network Structure and Community Formation
description: Papers developing or applying computational/graph-based methods to detect, map, and explain emergent structural patterns—communities, practice clusters, and transitive ties—in large-scale online social networks, using techniques such as self-supervised graph embeddings and causal network analysis.

name: Cultural Imaginaries and Framings of Generative AI
description: Papers examining how generative AI is culturally imagined, discursively framed, and theorized as a medium, ranging from newspaper coverage and Silicon Valley community discourse to media-theoretical accounts of AI's distinctive properties as a creative medium.
